extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and their attorneys/agents seeking expedited or special-status examination before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural standards for filing petitions to make a U.S. patent application "special" (including accelerated examination) and for the conduct of examination and prosecution under those programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for recombinant DNA safety inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord "special" status to patent applications relating to safety of research in the field of recombinant DNA upon appropriate petition and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h). Petitions should be accompanied by statements under 37 CFR 1.102 by the applicant, assignee, or statements by an attorney/agent explaining the relationship of the invention to safety of research in recombinant DNA research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be accompanied by fee and a statement explaining relationship to safety of recombinant DNA research. NIH is sponsoring experimental work to identify hazards and safety practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special — general formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to make special should be in writing and identify the application by application number and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions are entered into the application file with a paper number; decisions are given separate paper numbers. Petitions are decided by the Special Program Examiner of the assigned Technology Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for superconductivity inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord "special" status to all patent applications for inventions involving superconductivity materials on request. Such requests should be accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 that the invention involves superconductive materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include superconductive materials, their manufacture and application. No fee is required for such a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for HIV/AIDS and cancer inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord "special" status to patent applications relating to HIV/AIDS and cancer. Applicants should file a petition and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) requesting special status, accompanied by a statement explaining how the invention contributes to the diagnosis, treatment or prevention of HIV/AIDS or cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must state how the invention contributes to diagnosis/treatment/prevention; fee required under 37 CFR 1.17(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for inventions materially contributing to countering terrorism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord "special" status to patent applications for inventions which materially contribute to countering terrorism. Petition under 37 CFR 1.102 must state that special status is sought because the invention materially contributes to countering terrorism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is required. If disclosure is not clear, petition must be accompanied by a statement under 37 CFR 1.102 explaining how the invention materially contributes. Materiality does not permit speculation about hypothetical end-users or claiming benefit for a minor aspect of the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status for biotechnology applications filed by small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Small-entity applicants may request special status for biotechnology applications by filing a petition with fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) and must: (A) state that small entity status has been established or include a statement establishing it; (B) state that the subject is a major asset of the small entity; and (C) state that development will be significantly impaired if examination is delayed, with an explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include the three statements above to qualify. Fee is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination — petition and basic eligibility (R-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may be granted accelerated examination status if it is filed with a petition to make special under the accelerated examination program accompanied by either the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h) or a statement that the claimed subject matter is directed to environmental quality, development/conservation of energy resources, or countering terrorism. Applicant should use form PTO/SB/28.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/28 is recommended for petitions other than those based on health/age or PPH. Applications filed before Aug 25, 2006 are not eligible for this program (except health/age/PPH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination — application type eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be a non-reissue utility or design application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain filing types are expressly ineligible (see eligibility rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination — electronic filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The application, petition, and required fees must be filed electronically using the USPTO's electronic filing system (EFS) or EFS-Web. If EFS/EFS-Web is not available during normal business hours, filing by mail with a statement that EFS was unavailable is permitted but final disposition may occur later than twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing expedites processing; non-electronic filings risk delay beyond the 12-month goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination — condition for examination at filing (completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of filing, the application must be complete under 37 CFR 1.51 and in condition for examination — e.g., filed with the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, application size fee (if applicable), and an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application not in condition for examination at filing is not eligible and the opportunity to perfect the petition does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-count and claim-type limits for accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain three or fewer independent claims and twenty or fewer total claims, and must not contain any multiple dependent claims. By filing a petition, applicant agrees not to separately argue the patentability of any dependent claim during any appeal in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must include a statement agreeing not to separately argue dependent claims on appeal (see 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(vii)). Excess claims or multiple dependent claims will render the petition noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-invention requirement and election without traverse
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims must be directed to a single invention. If the Office determines the claims are not obviously to a single invention, applicant must make an election without traverse as a prerequisite to special status; the petition must include a statement that applicant will agree to make such an election in a telephonic interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant refuses to make an election without traverse, the application will not be further examined at that time and the petition will be denied. The telephone restriction practice will be followed if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must be willing to have an interview (including before a first Office action) to discuss prior art and any potential rejections/objections, with the intention of clarifying and possibly resolving issues; the petition must include a statement agreeing to such interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to arrange interviews during the shortened reply periods; applicants should provide proposed amendments at least one working day before an interview so the examiner can consider them (these preliminary papers do not become part of the file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preexamination search statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At filing applicant must provide a statement that a preexamination search was conducted, listing the field of search by class and subclass, publication, Chemical Abstracts, foreign patents, etc., and for database searches include search logic or chemical structure/sequence used, name of files/databases and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preexamination search must involve U.S. patents and patent application publications, foreign patent documents, and non-patent literature unless applicant justifies with reasonable certainty why elimination is permissible; it must be directed to the claimed invention and encompass all claim features under the broadest reasonable interpretation. A foreign patent office search report only satisfies this requirement if it meets these requirements. Statements must be made in good faith (see 37 CFR 1.56 and 10.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope coverage of preexamination search and consequences of uncovered amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The preexamination search must encompass the disclosed features that may be claimed. An amendment to the claims (including any new claim) that is not encompassed by the preexamination search or an updated accelerated examination support document will be treated as an improper reply and will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that broaden the search field are improper replies. Applicants must provide an updated support document when submitting amendments that change claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination support document (content requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must provide an accelerated examination support document including: (1) an IDS per 37 CFR 1.98 citing each reference deemed most closely related to the subject matter of each claim; (2) for each reference, identification of all claim limitations disclosed and where disclosed; (3) a detailed explanation of how each claim is patentable over the references with particularity required by 37 CFR 1.111(b) and (c); (4) a concise statement of the utility of the invention as defined in each independent claim; (5) a showing where each claim limitation finds support under the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 in the written description (and identification of corresponding structure/material/acts for means-plus-function elements under 112, para. 6, and in any priority applications); and (6) identification of any cited references that may be disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The support document is detailed and must map claim limitations to prior art and to the specification. Failure to include or defects in the document can cause denial of the petition; applicants may be given a single opportunity to perfect certain defects within one month (no extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on petition and opportunity to perfect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition or accelerated examination support document does not meet all requirements, applicant will be notified of defects and given a single opportunity (one month, no extensions) to perfect the petition/document unless the application was not in condition for examination on filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If perfected timely, the petition will be granted but final disposition may occur later than twelve months from filing. If not perfected in the first renewed petition, further renewals may be considered at TC discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial examiner action timing and pre-action conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Once granted special status the application will be docketed and taken up expeditiously (e.g., within two weeks). The USPTO will not issue an Office action (other than notice of allowance) unless (A) an interview was conducted but did not result in allowance, or (B) there is a determination that an interview is unlikely to result in allowance. Prior to mailing any Office action rejecting the claims, the USPTO will conduct a conference to review the rejections set forth in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are not to a single invention, telephone restriction practice will be followed and applicant must make an election without traverse during telephonic interview. If examiner cannot reach applicant, claim 1 may be constructively elected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory reply periods and no extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: A first action rejection will set a 3-month shortened period for reply; if an Office action other than allowance or final is mailed, it will set a shortened statutory period of one month or thirty days, whichever is longer. No extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are permitted; failure to timely reply will result in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the shortened periods to arrange interviews and resolve issues promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply content limits (responsiveness) in accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to an Office action must be restricted to the rejections, objections, and requirements made. Any amendment that would (A) add claims resulting in more than three independent or more than twenty total claims, (B) present claims not encompassed by the preexamination search or an updated support document, or (C) present claims directed to a nonelected invention, will be treated as not fully responsive and will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any amendment not encompassed by the support document, applicant must file an updated support document at the time of filing the amendment. IDS filed with updates must comply with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98. Replies and other papers must be filed electronically via EFS-Web to be expeditiously processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-allowance processing and fee/timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing of a notice of allowance is the final disposition for the twelve-month goal. Applicant must pay the issue fee within three months from mailing of the Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due (form PTOL-85) to avoid abandonment. To expedite issuance applicant must pay the issue fee (and any outstanding fees) within one month from mailing of PTOL-85 and must not file any post-allowance papers not required by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely pay issue fees or filing unnecessary post-allowance papers can cause delay or abandonment and harm the 12-month objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final, appeal, and RCE procedures while maintaining special status
rubrics_metrics.description: Mailing of a final Office action or filing of a notice of appeal is a final disposition for the twelve-month goal. Prior to mailing a final Office action the USPTO will conduct a conference. To expedite forwarding to the BPAI, applicant must promptly file the notice of appeal, appeal brief, and fees and must not request a pre-appeal brief conference. Filing an RCE is a final disposition for the twelve-month goal; the application retains special status after an RCE and the examiner will continue to examine under accelerated procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During appeal the application is treated under normal appeal procedures. The goal after an RCE is to reach final disposition within twelve months from filing the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings outside normal examination process
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application becomes involved in proceedings outside normal examination (e.g., secrecy order, national security review, interference, or certain petitions), the USPTO will treat the application as special before and after those proceedings but will not accelerate it during those proceedings. After such proceedings are completed the USPTO will process the application expeditiously under the accelerated program, though final disposition may be later than twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect normal processing during the special proceeding and resumed accelerated processing afterwards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility exclusions for accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are not eligible for the accelerated examination program: (1) plant applications; (2) reissue applications; (3) applications entering national stage after compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371; (4) reexamination proceedings; (5) RCEs under 37 CFR 1.114 (unless the application was previously granted special status under the program); and (6) petitions to make special based on applicant's health or age or under the PPH pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applicants may use the expedited examination program per MPEP § 1504.30 instead of accelerated examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PTO/SB/28 form
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should use form PTO/SB/28 for filing a petition to make special (other than those based on applicant's health or age or the PPH pilot program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form available on EFS-Web and the USPTO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed conditions for examination (items to be present at filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: At time of filing the application must include: (1) basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee; (2) application size fee if applicable; (3) executed oath/declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63; (4) specification with description and claims in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52/1.71/1.75; (5) title and abstract per 37 CFR 1.72; (6) drawings per 37 CFR 1.84; (7) electronic sequence listings/large tables/computer listings in ASCII via EFS if applicable; (8) foreign priority claim identified per 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) if applicable; (9) domestic benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78 if applicable; (10) English translation and accuracy statement and processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i) if specification is non-English; (11) no preliminary amendments present on filing date; and (12) no petition under 37 CFR 1.47 for a non-signing inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications must also comply with 37 CFR 1.151-1.154. Petition to make special will be dismissed if the application omits an item or includes a paper that causes formality-review notices. Applicants should provide suggested classification to expedite processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply not fully responsive — cure opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to a non-final Office action is not fully responsive but is a bona fide attempt to advance the application, the examiner may provide one month or thirty days, whichever is longer, for applicant to supply the omission or a fully responsive reply. No extensions are permitted. Failure to timely file the omission or a fully responsive reply will result in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional time will be given if the reply is not a bona fide attempt or if it is a reply to a final Office action. The prior time in the previous Office action continues to run.

rubrics_metrics.name: No withdrawal from accelerated status
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision for 'withdrawal' from special status under the accelerated examination program. An applicant may abandon the special-status application in favor of a continuing application, but the continuing application will not automatically receive special status unless filed with a petition under the accelerated examination program. Filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 will not withdraw an application from special status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve accelerated processing in a continuing application a new petition must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve-month goal objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the accelerated examination program is to complete the examination of an application within twelve months from the filing date of the application; success is achieved when certain final dispositions occur (e.g., notice of allowance, final action/appeal/RCE as described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several events constitute final disposition for the 12-month goal (see program rules); certain defects/permitted delays may cause final disposition to occur later than twelve months.
